## What you should be able to do tonight

- Reproduce the spurious regression result and its explanation without notes.
- State both unit root test nulls and the correct conclusion in all four outcome combinations.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>40 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 71 to 76. The ADF power curve is the piece most often skipped and the one most worth having, because it is what stops you from over-reading a failure to reject.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} One page, closed book: why the spurious t-statistic diverges, both test nulls with the four-outcome table, what Newey-West estimates, what differencing costs you, and why a structural break fails to reject a unit root. Then check and mark the misses.
:::
:::

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, eleventh sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 1/64, 1/128 and 1/256 as decimals.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Bayes with a base rate that moves: a coin is fair with probability 0.9 and biased to 0.75 heads otherwise. You see 8 heads in 10 flips. Posterior that it is biased? Set it up with likelihood ratios rather than with the full formula.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Expectation, geometric: on average, how many times do you have to roll a fair die to see all six faces? Get the answer by decomposing into six waiting times, then say the general formula for n faces and its growth rate.
:::
:::
